summary: Kang-yuan Sung is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned an MA at the University of Calgary, studying under Anthony W. Barber, Anne Moore, and Leslie S. Kawamura.

Kangei Okamoto (1899–1948) was a Buddhist studies and history/archaeology scholar. He studied under Takamatsu Yoshie, attended the University of Paris around 1928–1933, and held an appointment as嘱託 at Tokyo National Museum.
Kanji Tamura (born 1944) is a Buddhist studies scholar who has served at Rissho University as a part-time lecturer in Buddhist studies (attested 2001) and as an associate professor (attested 2026).
Kanoko Tanaka is a scholar in religious studies and Indology who studied under Acharya Tulsi. She served as a part-time lecturer in religious studies at Komazawa University (attested 2001).
Kansei Tamura (1928–2018) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and held a lectureship at Rissho University (both attested 1962).
Kanti Chandra Pandey (1903–1971) was an Indology and philosophy scholar who founded the University of Lucknow and held a post there (attested 1950).

Kapila Vatsyayan (1928–2020) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. She earned degrees from Delhi, Michigan, and Banaras Hindu universities, taught at Delhi and BHU, and co-founded and served as trustee, academic director, and chairperson of IGNCA.

Karam Tej Singh Sarao (born 1955) is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and history scholar. He studied at Panjab, Delhi, and Cambridge universities, and became a professor at the University of Delhi in 1995 alongside multiple international visiting appointments.

Karandagolle Sobhitha is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed an MPhil at the University of Peradeniya. He taught at Peradeniya (2011–2015) and served as Senior Lecturer in Sanskrit at Bhiksu University of Sri Lanka (2015–2021).
Karel Glaser (1845–1913) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Berlin and Vienna under Georg Bühler. He taught at Stadtgymnasium Trieste from 1880 to 1900.

Karel Oštir (1888–1973) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Vienna and Graz under Paul Kretschmer and Rudolf Meringer. From 1922 to 1958, he held academic positions, including Professor of IE Philology, at the University of Ljubljana.
Karel Přikryl (1718–1785) was an Indologist and linguist. He taught at Rachol Seminary around 1756–1761 and served as Rector at the Jesuit College in Hradec Králové in 1768.

Karel Werner (1925–2019) was a scholar of Indology, religion, and philosophy who founded Masaryk University and studied at Palacký and Masaryk. He taught at Palacký, Cambridge, and Masaryk, and lectured in Indian philosophy at Durham University (1969–1990).

Karen Christina Lang is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who studied at Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg, Banaras Hindu University, and the LTWA. She served as a professor at the University of Virginia.
Karen Katsumoto is a Buddhist studies scholar who has served as a part-time lecturer at Hanazono University (attested 2006) and at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2026).

Karen McCarthy Brown (1942–2015) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Smith College, Union Theological Seminary, and Temple University. She served as a professor of anthropology at Drew University from around 1976 to 2009.
Karen Nelson Villanueva is a religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies and studied under Geshe Ngawang Dakpa and Lobsang Chökyi.
Karen Nero is a scholar who held posts at the University of Canterbury (around 1998–2004) and the University of Otago.

Karen O'Brien-Kop is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from SOAS, lectured at the University of Roehampton (attested 2020), and became Lecturer in Modern Asian Religions at King's College London in 2022.

Karin Meyers is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Jay L. Garfield. She served as assistant professor and MA program director in Buddhist studies at Kathmandu University's Centre for Buddhist Studies at Rangjung Yeshe Institute.
